history.content: The Florence Cathedral, also known as the Cattedrale di Santa Maria del Fiore, is the mother church of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Florence, Italy. It is an important architectural structure, showcasing Italian Gothic, Renaissance, and Gothic Revival styles. The cathedral complex, which includes the Baptistery and Giotto's Campanile, is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site that encompasses the historic center of Florence. The cathedral's dome, designed by Filippo Brunelleschi, was the largest in the world until the advent of new structural materials in the modern era, and it remains the largest brick dome ever constructed.
Does it have artwork from Michelangelo?
I do not have specific information suggesting that Michelangelo has directly contributed artwork to the Florence Cathedral.
What artwork can we find in it?

Lorenzo Ghiberti had a significant artistic impact on the cathedral. He collaborated with Filippo Brunelleschi on the cathedral for eighteen years and worked on numerous projects, particularly at the eastern end. Some of his notable contributions include stained glass designs, the bronze shrine of Saint Zenobius, and the marble revetments on the exterior of the cathedral.
On top of the façade, there is a series of niches featuring the Twelve Apostles, with the Madonna and Child positioned in the center. Between the rose window and the tympanum, a gallery displays busts of renowned Florentine artists. 
Additionally, the beautiful funeral monument of Antonio d'Orso, the bishop of Florence (created in 1323), was crafted by Tino da Camaino, who was the most important funeral sculptor of his time. Interestingly, the decorations for the drum gallery, created by Baccio d'Agnolo, were never completed after being disapproved by none other than Michelangelo.
Have any significant historical events happened there?

Yes. This cathedral has served as the site of significant events throughout its long history, including the Council of Florence in 1439. It has also been a venue for the sermons of Girolamo Savonarola and was the location of the murder of Giuliano di Piero de' Medici on Sunday, April 26, 1478, during the Pazzi conspiracy, in which Lorenzo il Magnifico narrowly escaped death.

The cathedral, designed by Arnolfo di Cambio, was constructed in 1296 and completed in 1469 with the placement of Verrochio's copper ball atop the lantern. However, the façade remained unfinished until the 19th century.

The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson
Carson 's contract , that took effect in 1981 , reduced his work schedule to three nights a week , 37 weeks a year . `` Best of Carson '' reruns aired on Tuesdays in the weeks that Carson was hosting new shows .

Due to the frequent need for substitutes , starting in 1983 permanent guest hosts were hired in order to give the program more stability . The permanent guest hosts were Joan Rivers ( 1983 -- 86 ) , then , after about a year where a wide range of guest hosts were used , Garry Shandling alternating with Jay Leno ( 1987 - 88 ) and finally Leno alone ( 1988 -- 92 ) after Shandling left to focus on his Showtime series It 's Garry Shandling 's Show .
